_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for BMY retrospectives (retro/build_bmy.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2007-2009 were accepted before the open or during the session on their release days. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K; it also restates the year before when a business became a discontinued operation), the guides for the current fiscal year (each field from the latest guide that states it) and the latest declared dividend. Bristol-Myers Squibb's fiscal year is the calendar year. EPS is GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations: the company's non-GAAP EPS excludes upfront and milestone licensing payments, which recur, so it is shown and never used. 2001 is excluded and the history starts with 2002. A later year whose reported EPS is under half the EPS without the specified items its Q4 release lists, with no figure excluding only one-offs, is excluded the same way but stays reported ('eps_excluded' on a vintage; an 'excluded_note' and no EPS on the Q4 print's full-year actuals): 2015. Guides: GAAP EPS ranges (the current-FY EPS) and non-GAAP ranges (shown only); revenue growth is guided in words, so BASE takes the latest quarter's net sales growth excluding foreign exchange as each release states it, except where a release guides worldwide sales or revenues in dollars (FY2012-FY2015), read as growth on the last full year. A print's growth and margins are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw', $ millions; the builder re-derives and checks them), each against the year-ago quarter as the same release shows it; U.S. and international net sales come from the release's supplemental exhibit. Rule T's raw figures are in 'rule_t'. No later fact enters through this file: every source's published date bounds its use.

rule_t._doc: Rule T over fiscal 1997-2006, the decade of the FY2006 10-K (the vintage public on 2008-01-04): each year-on-year change from the latest 10-K (or 10-K/A) published by then that reports both years. U.S. and international net sales from the geographic data (international = the consolidated total less the United States; the FY1998 and FY1999 10-Ks state the United States before inter-area eliminations), the gross margin from the statements of earnings (net sales less cost of products sold), net sales growth and the pre-tax margin (earnings from continuing operations before minority interest and income taxes) from the five-year financial summaries. Seams stay in, as published: Clairol and Zimmer discontinued from the FY2000 10-K, the 2003 restatement (wholesaler inventory) in the FY2001 10-K/A and FY2002 10-K, the 2004 restatement in the FY2003 10-K/A, OTN discontinued from the FY2004 10-K, and 2001's acquired in-process research and development ($2,772 million, DuPont Pharmaceuticals) in its pre-tax earnings. Thresholds: XBULL the best year, BULL the median, BASE the worst, BEAR one median-to-worst step beyond the worst; whole percent and 10 bp, rounded half up.

price_basis: Yahoo's BMY series is adjusted for the 2-for-1 splits of 1997-03-03 and 1999-03-01 and books the 2001 Zimmer spin-off as a 1000000:951777 split on 2001-08-07; none follows 2001, so from 2002 Yahoo's close is the price as traded ($26.52 on 2007-12-31, the fourth-quarter 2007 low the FY2007 10-K reports). No per-share fact in this file was published before the 1999 split (every history year comes from a filing of 2003 or later), so 'splits' is empty; the spin-off factor is a 'distributions' record.
